thread:
Nina: quick follow-up on the ephemeral padding idea from the autoscale RFC. want to decide who converts time->slots and how preemption should behave.
Omar: quick summary please?
Nina: padding = very short-lived capacity added on bursts (20-40s). goal: cut 95p cold-starts for bursty tenants with minimal extra GPU-hours.
Priya: main choice: control-plane computes exact tokens (global fairness) or operator converts a time hint into slots (better packing).
Omar: operator conversion wins for packing but we need caps set by control-plane to avoid cost spikes.
Nina: propose control-plane sends hint {padding_secs, max_padding_pct, priority_weight}. operator returns allocation with fields: allocated_slots, padding_slots, expiry_ts, preemptible=true.
Ravi: preemption: padding_slots are first-to-preempt, short grace (2-5s), no checkpointing. mark workloads as "padding" to exclude from steady SLOs.
Priya: add absolute expiry_ts on allocations so reconciliation is idempotent across operator restarts.
Omar: metric signal: EWMA(1m) baseline + burst detector (10s window, multiplier 3) to trigger padding. sizing: ceil(EWMA_rate * target_latency_s * safety) floored to 1, capped by commit * max_padding_pct.
DevOps-bot: canary note: applied padding_secs=25, max_padding_pct=0.10 to autoscaler-canary at 2024-11-07T07:10Z.
Ravi: observability: emit events IntentCreated, AllocationAck, PaddingExpired, PaddingPreempted with tenant and ids. Console needs split billing tags so product can show padding cost.
Priya: testing: run synthetic 30s spikes across 1k tenants; track 95p cold-start vs padding GPU-hours. target <12% extra hours for >=50% reduction in cold starts.
Nina: action items: Omar to prototype operator conversion + expiry logic. Priya to add Console billing tag mock. Ravi to wire events. I'll run canary and report back next week.
Omar: +1, will post branch.
Nina: thanks all :thumbsup:
